segments.he:
תּוֹרָה קלז
הַחֵלֶק אֱלֹהִי מִמַּעַל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לִי אוֹמֵר לִי וּמְלַמֵּד אוֹתִי לִשְׁמֹר כִּדְבָרֶיךָ:
segments.en:
Major themes across this section:

Joy and the Shechinah (T89–T90): The paradox: knowing one's deficiencies affect the Shechinah could cause debilitating sadness — but the antidote is to see the honour in the King confiding His own deficiency to you. And joy in G-d directly repairs the Shechinah's deficiencies.

Faith and intellect as a spiral (T91): Faith leads to intellectual understanding — but each attainment of understanding reveals higher matters requiring renewed faith. The ascent has no ceiling.

Faithful commerce (T93): Trading in faithfulness fulfils the root of all commandments — "and you shall love" — and elevates one above time, enabling clear prayer.

Holy eyes (T94): Faith + wisdom = a holy eye that elevates sparks from every object, forming holy words that channel G-d's blessing to Israel. Words are the vessels of abundance.

The Tzadik's prayer-power (T97): Every Jew can rule through prayer — but arrogance (from lineage or from spiritual achievement) blocks it. The solution: stand before prayer as if newborn, alone, with no history.

The blemish of faith mid-prayer (T108): Falling mid-prayer or mid-hisbodidus comes from a faith-blemish. The remedy: heartbreak, shame, sighing — and the sigh lifts one back.

The holy sigh (T109): More powerful than mortifications and fasts — a sigh over spiritual distance literally makes one a new creation.

Torah is spiritual / forgetting (T110): Torah occupies no space — a pure spiritual intellect retains everything. Materialising Torah causes forgetting.

One true word (T112): The extraordinary counsel — pray all one's life for one single true word spoken before G-d. Through this, one remains viable throughout all of life's descents, for truth is G-d's own light which no darkness can extinguish, and every spiritual prison has openings visible by that light.

Never complete the decree (T113): The Ba'al Shem Tov's teaching: before a decree is issued against a person, the person himself is consulted and unwittingly rules against himself. One must be extremely careful never to finalise a judgment about another's situation.

Complete teshuvah through Torah (T105): Genuine teshuvah is not achieved through mortifications but through Torah innovation — deriving one matter from another for Heaven's sake. This recreates the person entirely and ultimately causes G-d Himself to pray on one's behalf.

The coin before the eyes (T133): One of the most vivid parables in the Kitzur — the small coin held close to the eye blocking a great mountain. The vanities of this world block the vast light of Torah and Tzadikim only because they are so close. Move them aside — and the great mountain is immediately visible.

Binding to the Tzadik (T123): The foundation of foundations — one must discard all independent wisdom and bind oneself completely to the Tzadik's words. Any retained personal intellect means the bond is incomplete. This was the nature of Matan Torah itself.

Translation in the merit of Na Nach Nachma Nachman MayUman  ·  May Hashem bless all who learn from it.

  נ נח נחמ נחמן מאומן
